jamie: Quick check — Q2 forecasting ask for the vector-store + rerank workloads. We have the May promo (expected ~40% query spike for 2 weeks) and need a plan that minimizes on-demand cost. Can we avoid spinning a full extra dedicated pool?

sanjay: Short answer: probably, if we accept a mix of a larger preemptible batch pool + a small warmed realtime pool and shift heavy rerank batch to our off-peak window. Did a quick calc.

sanjay: Baseline weekly consumption (current):
- realtime rerank: ~2.2k GPU-hours/week (small instances, low qps but tight tail)
- embeddings batch: ~4.8k GPU-hours/week (overnight backfills + nightly indexing)

sanjay: Promo +40% QPS for two weeks -> peak week estimate:
- realtime rerank: 3.1k GPU-hours/week
- embeddings batch: 6.7k GPU-hours/week (if we keep same batch cadence)

lia: Could we shift more batch into the 03:00-09:00 UTC window to use existing spot capacity? That buys ~30-40% more batch GPU-hours per day if we extend window and accept some latency on indexing.

frida: FYI eu-west2 has a regional network egress throttling change next month. If we increase cross-region spillover we'll hit packets/sec limits and see 5-10% tail latency regressions for KV lookups. Need fallback routing or local cache pre-warm.

mateo: Cost quick math: using mixed spot/on-demand for the peak week vs adding a dedicated extra pool (64 GPUs on-demand) -> rough delta:
- Mixed (add 128 spot GPUs, 12h/day): +$18k/week (spots + pre-warm overhead)
- Dedicated 64 on-demand 24/7: +$48k/week
So mixed is substantially cheaper but riskier for tail SLOs.

jamie: Risk tradeoffs sound clear. SLO: p95 < 120ms for rerank calls. Can spot interruption-induced cold starts push p95 above that?

sanjay: If we rely on spot for realtime, yes. But we can do small always-on low-latency pool (8-16 GPUs) for the tail and use spot for throughput. Strategy:
- small pinned pool (12 GPUs) for p95 and KV cache residency
- large spot-backed autoscaling pool for throughput bursts (up to 256 GPUs)
- batch-only pools shifted into off-peak window to free capacity

lia: Also recommend warm-up policy: keep KV cache fill jobs running 30m before promo start, and use short-lived canary traffic to keep kernels hot. Ops runbook to pre-warm across eu/us regions.

frida: For network constraint in eu-west2, plan: set priority routing to local caches, and if spillover to us-west happens, route only low-priority indexing traffic. I'll open a PR to update the mesh fallback policy.

mateo: One more: if we increase spot reliance we should buy additional preemption-insurance (concurrency headroom) of ~15% capacity to maintain p95 at scale. That increases spot cost by ~6-8% but reduces failovers.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pool config applied to staging: cluster=vec-rerank-staging, pool=small-hot-12, target=12 GPUs.

jamie: Action items / owners:
- frida: push mesh fallback PR for eu-west2 network limits (ETA: today EOD)
- sanjay + lia: finalize weeks-of-peak runbook + pre-warm script (ETA: tomorrow)
- mateo: update cost model with 15% headroom scenario and spot insurance numbers (ETA: EOD)
- ops-bot/infra: schedule pre-warm job for 2026-05-01 02:30 UTC (ops-bot scheduled)

lia: Quick config snippet I'm proposing for HPA/autoscaler (pseudo):
```
patch: autoscaler:
  minReplicas: 3  # small-hot pool ~12 GPUs
  maxReplicas: 256 # allow spot bursts
  metrics:
    - type: RPS
      target: 1000
```

jamie: Thanks — if everyone can ack, we'll lock the mixed-strategy (small hot pool + spot burst + shifted batch) and run a practice pre-warm next week. :thumbsup:

sanjay: Ack. I'll also generate a short simulation (90% percentile of our synthetic traffic) to validate p95 with 15% headroom.

frida: Ack, opening PR now.

mateo: Ack, will send numbers to the finance slack for sign-off.

lia: Ack, will put the runbook into ./runbooks/vec-rerank-prewarm.md and link it here once done.

jamie: Perfect. Closing thread after the PR and the simulation results are in.
